title: STUDY TOPIC The Spirit in the life of Jesus part 15
devotional:
The role of the Holy Spirit in the Ministry of Jesus (Luke 4 14-30)

Jesus chose to preach this sermon to those who thought they knew him best.

Why would he do that?

He was teaching us that through the presence and power of the Spirit, God can use a life even though others may think very little of it.

Initially everyone was amazed at his teaching, however that soon changed!!

‘’All spoke well of him and were amazed at the gracious words that came from his lips. “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?” they asked. Luke 4 v22

‘Isn’t this Joseph’s son?’

If we were to think about this, this must have taken a lot of courage on Jesus’ part. Those who knew him the longest, refused to take him seriously. Joseph’s kid, nothing special about him! They reacted in amazement to His words in the synagogue, and then they began to remind themselves of their personal history with him: they were saying, “Jesus is the son of the local carpenter; He’s common, like us. Where does He get the idea that He’s something special? The Messiah will not be a tradesman!” the Rabbi's taught.

This was a significant moment in the life of Jesus. In the face being rejected, disregarded and not been taking seriously by his community, he allowed himself to be

influenced more by the work of the Spirit in his life, than the wrong opinions, lack of understanding and the insults of others. The courage that he needed to do what His Father asked of him, came from his life in the Spirit.

If we continually live out of our insecurities, and have a constant need for the approval and praise of others to give us significance and worth, then we have a spiritual problem, and we will find it more difficult to find the courage we need to accomplish God’s will.

‘’All the people in the synagogue were furious when they heard this. They got up, drove him out of the town, and took him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw him off the cliff. But he walked right through the crowd and went on his way.’’ Luke 4 v 28-30

Even though Jesus’ ministry was Spirit led, that didn’t guarantee success or effectiveness. Jesus’ rejection in Nazareth was a shadow of His cross, a very painful experience, as those whom He loved and grew up with, turned their backs on Him and even tried to kill him by threatening to throw Him over the cliff. The Spirit empowered ministry was the same spirit that would bring Him comfort in His ministry and enable Him to continue.
prayer: Father please help me to bring everything before you even my hurt and disappointments.
